newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: POLL - Iberian bond spreads set to widen on Bund.
newsitem.headline: POLL - Iberian bond spreads set to widen on Bund.

text.p: The spreads between Iberia's 10-year cash bonds and German Bunds look set to widen again during the summer with the return of nervousness over U.S. interest rates and doubts about Europe's single currency plans, according to analysts' forecasts.
A Reuter poll of analysts pointed to the gap narrowing again in the autumn with the differential ending the year below current levels.
However, the real advance will only be registered in the spring of 1998 when it became clear that these countries had made the grade for economic and monetary union (EMU).

The average forecast was for a spread of 70 basis points (bps) above the Bund for the Portuguese bond (OT) at the end of the year, with the Spanish Bono at around 99 bps over the Bund at the end of December.
The median forecast was also for 70 basis points for the OT by December, while the Bono would be at 78 basis points, a differential more in keeping the usual gap between Spain and Portugal.

The Portuguese 10-year cash bond is presently trading at an 86 basis point premium to the Bund, six basis points above its all-time low of 80 set in January. The Bono was at 94, 10 basis points above its minimum set at a time when international euphoria about the chances of southern European countries qualifying for EMU was at its height.
The poll of 12 analysts for the Portuguese market and nine for the Spanish bonds was carried out April 7-11.

"In the summer, there could be a widening (of the spreads) with an eventual U.S. rate rise and some crisis (of confidence) over EMU leading to profit-taking in the Iberian bonds," said analyst Giovanni Polastri of 4Cast in Londres.
"At the moment there is optimism about EMU due to the fact that (Helmut) Khol decided to stand in the (German) elections and the (recent) meeting (of Ecofin)", he said.
This analyst saw a spread of 110 basis points for the OT and 120 bps for the Bono in June before the gap narrowed to 70 and 80 bps, respectively, in December.

"The actual spread (Bonos/Bund) is low and close to the likely lows for the year. If, by chance, it touched 85 I would short Spain against Germany," said analyst Henrik Lumholdt of Bank of America in Madrid.
Nevertheless, there were dissenting voices. Manuel Matos of Banco Mello de Investimentos in Lisbon did not see any great widening of spreads.

"I do not see the spreads widening. The rise in the German yields is going to be greater than for Portugal and Spain," he said. "The convergence factor is in fact going to ensure that there is a slight, steady narrowing of spreads (during the year)," he added.
Matos saw a spread of 60 bps for the OT and 70 for the Bono at end-year, anticipating the average of the forecasts which were for these levels only to be reached next spring.
The average forecast of the poll was for the OT spread to stand at 60 basis points in March, 1998, with the Bono at 84. By the end of next year, the gap would be 27 and 53, respectively.
The median saw 60 for both countries in March, 1998, and 23 and 30 at end-December 1998.
"For 1998, the base scenario is that both countries will enter (EMU), even if we still think it will be a 'political' decision on membership," said Matos.
The decision on which European Union countries will join EMU from its launch in January, 1999, will be taken next spring.

"Our hypothesis is that Portugal will form part of EMU and therefore from March 1998, the spread should only reflect the difference in terms of liquidity between the two markets (OT/Bund)," said analyst Ana Paula Carvalho of Banco Portugues de Investimento (BPI).
This analyst saw the spread with the Bunds narrowing to just 10 basis points once Portugal had been given the green light to join the single currency.
--Lisbon bureau 3511-3150035
